TRUTH.title: The no-yes-man prompt
TRUTH.intro: Most AI assistants agree with you the moment you push back, even when you're wrong. Paste this at the start of a chat (or into your custom instructions) and it will tell you when you're wrong.

prompts.name: Paste at the start of any chat
prompts.text:
For this whole conversation, be an honest expert, not a cheerleader.
- If I say something wrong, tell me plainly and explain why, even if I push back.
- Don't open with praise like "Great question" or "You're absolutely right".
- When you're not sure, say how sure you are (for example: about 70% sure) and what would change your mind.
- If I disagree with you, only change your answer if I give you a new fact or a better argument. Repeating myself is not a reason.
Reply "Understood" and wait for my first question.

prompts.name: The 2-second test
prompts.text: I think [your claim]. Before you answer, list the 3 strongest reasons I might be wrong, then give your honest verdict in one line.

TRUTH.tip: Try it with a wrong fact on purpose. A good setup says "No, and here's why".

HUMAN.title: Sound like you, not like AI
HUMAN.intro: The words that give AI writing away, and a prompt that rewrites any text so it sounds like a person wrote it.

prompts.name: The rewrite prompt
prompts.text:
Rewrite the text below so it sounds like me talking to a colleague.
Rules:
- Short sentences. Contractions (I'm, don't, it's).
- No dashes of any kind. Use full stops or commas.
- Never use these words: delve, tapestry, testament, leverage, seamless, robust, elevate, embark, realm, journey, navigate, crucial, pivotal, foster, unlock, in today's fast-paced world, I hope this email finds you well, warm regards, furthermore, moreover.
- No intro, no summary at the end, no bullet points unless I had them.
- Keep my meaning and my facts. Don't add anything new.
Text:
[paste here]

prompts.name: Your voice, saved
prompts.text: Here are 3 messages I wrote myself: [paste 3 of your own emails or texts]. Describe my writing style in 5 short rules. From now on, write everything for me using those rules.

HUMAN.tip: The fastest check: read it out loud. If you wouldn't say it, cut it.

SHORT.title: Short answers, every time
SHORT.intro: Asked for one line and got five headings and a table? These two prompts fix that for good.

prompts.name: Put this in your custom instructions
prompts.text: Answer in the fewest words that fully answer the question. Default to 1 to 3 sentences. No headings, tables or bullet points unless I ask. No "Great question", no summary at the end, and don't offer to expand. If the question truly needs more, give the short answer first, then ask if I want detail.

prompts.name: For one question
prompts.text: Answer in one sentence of under 20 words. No preamble. [your question]

SHORT.tip: Custom instructions live in your AI app's settings (often called Personalisation or Instructions). Set it once and every chat follows it.

FIX.title: Change only what I asked
FIX.intro: Asked your AI to fix one typo and it rewrote everything? This prompt keeps it on a leash.

prompts.name: The surgical edit
prompts.text:
Make ONLY this change: [describe the change].
Do not change any other word, line, format or punctuation.
Return the full text with the change made, then list exactly what you changed as: line, before, after.
If you think something else should change, tell me after the list instead of doing it.
Text:
[paste here]

prompts.name: Check its work
prompts.text: Compare your version with my original word by word. List every difference. If there is any difference I didn't ask for, undo it and give me the corrected version.

FIX.tip: Works for CVs, code, captions and emails. The "list what you changed" line is what keeps it honest.

MEMORY.title: Make it stop repeating the mistake
MEMORY.intro: It says sorry, then does the same thing again. Here's how to give your AI a rule it actually keeps.

prompts.name: A rules block for the start of a chat
prompts.text:
Before you answer anything in this chat, read these rules. Check every answer against them before you send it.
RULES:
1. My name is spelled [Meera]. Never [Mira].
2. [your rule]
3. [your rule]
At the end of each answer, write "Rules checked". If you broke one, fix it before sending.

prompts.name: When it gets it wrong again
prompts.text: You made the same mistake again: [mistake]. Don't apologise. Quote the rule you broke, explain in one line why it happened, then give the corrected version.

MEMORY.tip: Long chats make AI forget early instructions. If a chat gets long, start a new one and paste the rules block first.

MUM.title: AI words, explained for Mum and Papa
MUM.intro: Ten AI words your parents keep hearing, each in one line they'll actually understand. Send this to the family group.

prompts.name: The cheat sheet
prompts.text:
PROMPT: your order. Like at a tea stall: "cutting chai, less sugar, extra ginger" gets you exactly that. Clearer order, better answer.
TOKEN: the AI reads in small pieces, like puris. Every piece is counted. Long messages use more.
HALLUCINATION: the AI makes something up and sounds sure, like the uncle at every wedding. Always double check facts, medicines and money.
MEMORY: in a long chat it forgets the start, like a family group with 300 unread messages. Start a new chat and say who you are.
MODEL: the cook. Same kitchen, different cook, different taste.
AGENT: an AI that can also press the buttons: book, send, pay. Only let it do what you'd let a stranger do.
DEEPFAKE: a fake video or voice that looks and sounds real.
VOICE CLONE: a fake call that sounds like your son or daughter asking for money. Hang up and call them back on their real number.
TRAINING: how the AI learned, by reading a huge library of text.
CHATBOT: the app you type to, like the one you're using.

prompts.name: Ask your AI to explain anything like this
prompts.text: Explain [AI word] to my 60-year-old mother in 2 sentences, using an everyday Indian example. No English jargon.

MUM.tip: The voice clone line is the one that matters most. Make sure they read that one.

SHOP.title: 5 prompts to run a small shop with AI
SHOP.intro: The five jobs the committee did for Mitti this week, as prompts you can use for your own shop, whatever you sell.

prompts.name: 1. Price it
prompts.text: I sell [product] made from [materials]. It costs me [cost] to make and takes [time]. Similar products sell for [prices you've seen]. My buyers are [who]. Suggest 3 prices (budget, fair, premium) with one line on who each one is for. Be honest if my cost is too high.

prompts.name: 2. The product description
prompts.text: Write a product description for [product] in under 40 words. Say what it is, who it's for and one detail that makes it different. No fancy words. Then give me 3 short titles.

prompts.name: 3. The post that sells
prompts.text: Write 3 short Instagram captions to sell [product] for [festival or occasion]. Each under 25 words, with one clear reason to buy now. No hashtag walls, max 3 hashtags.

prompts.name: 4. Answer the customer
prompts.text: A customer asked: "[their message]". Our real facts: [delivery time, price, stock]. Write a friendly reply under 40 words. Only promise what's in our facts.

prompts.name: 5. The review reply
prompts.text: Write a warm, short reply to this review: "[review]". Thank them by name, mention one detail from the review, no discount offers.

SHOP.tip: Prompt 4 is the one that saves you: "only promise what's in our facts" stops the AI inventing free gift wrap.

SAFE.title: The family safety message (AI scams)
SAFE.intro: Fake calls in your child's voice and fake videos of famous people are real now. Send this to your parents and agree a code word on the phone, never in the comments.

prompts.name: Send this to the family group
prompts.text:
Important, please read 🙏
Scammers can now copy our voices with AI and make fake videos of famous people.
1. If anyone calls in our voice asking for money, ask for our family code word. No code word, no money.
2. Hang up and call back on the number you already have saved.
3. Never share an OTP, PIN or bank details on a call, even if the voice sounds like us.
4. A famous face promising to double your money is always fake.
5. When in doubt, wait 10 minutes and call one of us. Scammers hate waiting.

prompts.name: Make it in your family language
prompts.text: Rewrite this safety message in simple [Hindi / your language] for my parents, warm and short, keeping all 5 points: [paste the message above]

SAFE.tip: Agree the code word in person or on a call. Never post it, and never send it in the family group.

JOB.title: What AI can and can't do in your job: the 15-minute check
JOB.intro: AI takes tasks, not whole jobs. This prompt sorts your week into what to hand over, what to keep, and what to learn next.

prompts.name: The check
prompts.text:
My job: [title, industry, country].
Here are the tasks I did last week: [list 10 to 15 tasks with rough hours].
For each task, tell me: (a) can AI do most of it today, partly, or not really, and why in one line, (b) which free or common tool would help.
Then: the 3 tasks I should hand to AI first, the 3 parts of my job that are hardest to replace and why, and 2 skills to learn in the next 30 days to be worth more. Be honest, not reassuring.

prompts.name: The 30-day plan
prompts.text: Turn those 2 skills into a 30-day plan: 30 minutes a day, free resources only, one small proof I can show my manager at the end.

JOB.tip: Use real tasks from your calendar, not your job description. The answer is only as good as the list.

BOSS.title: 5 polite replies for after-hours messages
BOSS.intro: Short, friendly, and they don't start work at 11 pm. Plus a prompt to make your own.

prompts.name: Copy one
prompts.text:
1. Got it, I'll pick this up first thing tomorrow.
2. Thanks for flagging. I'll have it to you by [time] tomorrow.
3. Noted! I'm offline now, will look at it at 9.
4. On it tomorrow morning. Is anything here truly urgent tonight?
5. Sure. Can it wait till tomorrow, or should I flag it to [name] tonight?

prompts.name: Write your own
prompts.text: My boss messaged at [time]: "[message]". I want to reply kindly, not start work now, and give a clear time I will do it. Give me 3 options under 15 words each. No apologies.

BOSS.tip: Reply 4 is the quiet hero: it asks them to decide whether it is really urgent.

GIFT.title: The gift finder prompt
GIFT.intro: For bosses, in-laws and the cousin you barely know. A real shortlist inside your budget, not a smart watch that spies on them.

prompts.name: The prompt
prompts.text: Suggest 5 gift ideas for my [relation, e.g. boss], [age], who likes [2 or 3 things]. Occasion: [Diwali]. Budget: under [₹1,000] including delivery. City: [city]. Each idea: what it is, rough price, why it suits them, and one way it could go wrong. Nothing too personal for a [work / family] relationship.

prompts.name: The card
prompts.text: Write a 2-line card for this gift to my [relation]. Warm, not over the top, no more than 25 words.

GIFT.tip: Ask for "one way it could go wrong" every time. It catches the awkward gifts.

WISH.title: Diwali wishes that sound like you
WISH.intro: Personal wishes for a whole list of people in two minutes, without sounding like a forward or writing a book.

prompts.name: The prompt
prompts.text:
Write Diwali wishes for these people. Each one 1 or 2 short lines, in my voice (casual, warm, a little funny), using the one detail I give. No "sparkling", no "may this festival of lights", no emoji walls, max one emoji.
1. [Name] - [relation] - [one detail: a memory, a joke, what they did this year]
2. ...
3. ...

prompts.name: Mixed languages
prompts.text: Now write the same wishes in natural Hinglish, the way I would text them.

WISH.tip: The one detail per person is what makes it feel personal. Without it, you get a forward.

HIKE.title: The one-page wins list for your appraisal
HIKE.intro: Most people walk into an appraisal with nothing but a feeling. This turns your year into one page of wins with numbers, in about 20 minutes, using your own mail, calendar and notes.
steps: Search your sent mail for the last 12 months with words like done, shipped, launched, fixed, thank you, plus your manager's name.
Scroll your calendar for launches, reviews and client meetings you led.
Pick your 5 biggest wins and give each one a number: hours saved, customers, deadlines met, errors fixed.
Fit them on one page, then add one line on what you want to take on next year.
Bring any public salary survey only as context, and keep the tone calm and factual.

prompts.name: Find my wins
prompts.text: Here are notes and messages from my work this year: [paste, with confidential names and numbers removed]. Find the 5 biggest things I did. For each one, write a single line: what I did and the result, with a number if one is given. If there is no number, ask me for it instead of guessing. Do not invent anything.

prompts.name: Make it one page
prompts.text: Turn these 5 wins into a one-page appraisal summary in plain English, under 200 words, with no buzzwords and no headings except 'My year'. Wins: [paste].

prompts.name: Prepare the conversation
prompts.text: I have an appraisal meeting soon. My wins: [paste]. Write 3 short, calm sentences I can open with, then the 3 questions my manager is most likely to ask, each with an honest answer I could give. Keep it polite and confident, not pushy.

HIKE.tip: Don't paste confidential company data into a personal AI account. Remove client names and internal figures first.

SPACE.title: Free up your Google storage in 15 minutes
SPACE.intro: When the free 15 GB is full, photos stop backing up and your email can stop sending and receiving. Here is how to clear the biggest files first, for free.
steps: Back up anything precious first: download it, or export it with Google Takeout.
Open the Google storage manager (link below) and review 'Large items' first.
In Gmail, search has:attachment larger:10M, then delete the emails you don't need.
Delete old videos and screen recordings in Photos. They take far more space than pictures.
Empty the Bin in Gmail, Drive and Photos. Deleted files still count until the Bin is emptied.

prompts.name: Sort what to delete
prompts.text: I am freeing up storage. Here is a list of my largest files and emails with their sizes: [paste]. Sort them into three groups: safe to delete, check first, keep. Put anything that looks like an ID, a document or a family photo in 'keep' unless I say otherwise.

prompts.name: Build my search lines
prompts.text: Write 5 Gmail search lines that find big or old emails I can probably delete, for example newsletters or attachments older than 2 years. Use real Gmail operators such as has:attachment, larger:, older_than: and category:. Explain each one in a single short line.

SPACE.tip: Sort by size, not by date. Twenty big files free more space than two thousand small ones.

OFFER.title: Is this job offer real? The 10-minute check
OFFER.intro: Fake offers reach freshers and job hunters on WhatsApp and Telegram every day. Run these checks before you pay anything or share any documents.
steps: A fee to join, train or 'verify documents' is the biggest warning sign. Real employers do not charge one.
Look the company up for free on mca.gov.in under MCA Services, View Company/LLP Master Data (a free login may be needed). Check that the name, registered address and status match the letter.
Find the company's own website yourself and contact HR from there. Never use the number or link printed in the offer.
Be wary if the email comes from a free email address instead of the company's own domain.
No interview, pressure to pay today, or a recruiter who only chats? Stop there.
If you have paid or shared bank details, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in straight away.

prompts.name: Red flag check
prompts.text: Here is a job offer I received: [paste, with my personal details removed]. List every warning sign of a fake job offer that you can see in it, then list what I should verify myself on official sources. Do not tell me for certain that it is real or fake. Tell me what to check.

prompts.name: Ask HR to confirm
prompts.text: Write a short, polite email to a company's official HR address asking them to confirm whether this offer letter is genuine. Mention the role, the date on the letter and the name of the sender. Five lines maximum.

OFFER.tip: Treat any rush to pay as the scam itself. Real jobs wait while you check.

SCAM.title: The 60-second fake check: links, screenshots and PIN requests
SCAM.intro: Most money scams use one of three tricks: a link that promises free money, a fake 'payment done' screenshot, or a request for your PIN. Here is what to do with each one.
steps: A 'free money' or government bonus forward? Don't tap the link. Send it to PIB Fact Check on WhatsApp at +91 8799711259 or email factcheck@pib.gov.in. They check claims about the government.
Report the scam message or call on Chakshu, inside the Sanchar Saathi portal or app.
Selling online? Ship only when the money shows in your own bank or UPI app history. A screenshot can be edited.
Your UPI PIN is only for sending money. Nobody needs it for you to receive money.
If money has gone, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in at once.

prompts.name: Is this real?
prompts.text: Here is a message I received: [paste]. Do not tell me whether it is real. List the warning signs you can see, and tell me which official website or helpline I should use to check it myself.

prompts.name: Reply to the family group
prompts.text: Write a short, kind message for my family group saying this forward is fake and nobody should tap the link, without embarrassing the person who sent it. Three lines, simple English with a little Hindi.

prompts.name: Seller payment line
prompts.text: Write a friendly two-line message to a buyer saying that I ship as soon as the payment shows in my own account, and that I don't ship on screenshots.

SCAM.tip: Anything that rushes you ('today only', 'cut tonight', 'offer ends in 1 hour') is your cue to slow down.
